revised.summary:
Show Bus 1.3, revised after review. The full design is at /home/user/Stagewatch/docs/ecosystem/spec-1-3.md. The first draft is kept at <scratch>/spec13-rev/spec-1-3.v1.md, and §11 of the design answers every review item.

The 1.3 master now:
- names PlayMap: the `playmap` kind, its caps and a §8 row;
- defines `proto` as the revision whose message shapes a node speaks, with each node's §8 row listing what it does not keep yet;
- gives one table of numbers. Senders stay at or under each number and readers accept at least it. Context is 64 KiB, 200 items and 400 links (Patterns already writes 200), and a reader that keeps commands keeps at least 256. When a context is too big, the sender trims it in a fixed order;
- says where a hello goes. A node sends it from a socket bound to the address its doors listen on. Nobody relies on the extra copy sent to 127.0.0.1, because on a shared port only one listener receives it (measured again here). A node bound to loopback only sends no hello;
- says how a peer is heard. One id is one peer, with every address it was heard from, and the link keeps dialling the same address while it is still heard. One id heard from two running copies of an app is shown amber and never merged;
- states the rule that show state is read only after pairing, and lists each node's exceptions;
- counts a certificate's whole span (825 days) and replaces one already issued that is longer, once;
- adds §12.1-12.3: what a window is, view passes (window addresses, viewing codes, crew links), and the window link as it already works. Grants are written by the windows-for-peers area.

Every copy carries the same body, held by a hash. Each tree's test stops accidental edits to its own copy; only the cross-tree interop lane finds a copy that is older than the master.

What the operator gains:
- Stagewatch's hello never names a door the network cannot open, and goes silent when Remote is set to this PC.
- A hello that fails is shown on the desk. A failure lights amber only when every target fails.
- A peer's address stops flipping every second.
- An app copied to a second machine with the same id is named amber instead of silently merged.
- PlayMap is named everywhere.
- Existing certificates are replaced once, so iPads keep trusting them.
- Wrong window addresses no longer lock out the PIN, and a correct key no longer resets the window-address count.
- How apps on one laptop with no network find each other is measured on Windows (lab line LB-1) before the contract promises it. Until then a typed 127.0.0.1 address works.

What each app gains:
- **Stagewatch:** a pure, tested hello builder that reads the settings snapshot; per-target send counts; a hello listener that keeps every address per id and detects id conflicts; certificate life rules; separate view-pass lockouts; NODES.md rebuilt from the code and held by a test; a probe for LB-1.
- **Patterns:** one Round 90 brings the 825-day certificate, the 1.3 hello and hearing rules, and the copy. If its maintainer agrees (ADR-016), it also brings state shown only after pairing. That includes the Companion module pairing before it reads and pairing state kept per connection, so changing the token stops the pushes.
- **AGMessage:** the 825-day span and the one renewal; a hello sent from HOST; peer lookup that keeps working on one laptop; 32 caps; a spec test.
- **PlayMap:** room for more caps, its §5 proposals answered, a copy and a test once round 3 allows. Whether its TCP wire should read only after pairing is put to its owner as a question.

decisions.decision: One owner edits the master, and every area that changes it hands over its words: playout-links, cross-app-proposals, peers-not-screens, windows-for-peers, agmessage, ecosystem-lane and patterns-playmap-side. This area writes §1 rule 4, rule 5's view-pass class, §2, §4, §6 sizes, trimming and posting, §7.2, §8's table and exemptions, §9, §10, §12.1-12.3, §13 and the copy rule.
decisions.why: One hash per revision. Seven areas name master words (design/windows-for-peers.md:553-573, design/agmessage.md:472-475, design/ecosystem-lane.md:591-597, design/patterns-playmap-side.md:494-504).
decisions.alternatives: Each area edits its own sections. Rejected because of the copy fence and merge noise.

decisions.decision: PlayMap joins as kind `playmap` with every cap it sends, plus a §8 row. Its seven §5 proposals are answered one by one: kind and caps adopted; the device link and third-party contexts are Patterns' Round 92; the destination is not contract; the finder belongs to playout-links; `video.anchor` is reserved; commands follow §6's rule.
decisions.why: A word enters the contract when a node sends it and its meaning is fixed.

decisions.decision: `proto` is the revision whose shapes a node speaks: 1 = 1.1, 2 = 1.2, 3 = 1.3, and it only grows. What a node does not keep yet is in its §8 row with what ends it. Readers never refuse a hello because of its proto and never make a safety decision on it. A node that shows nothing before pairing is recognised by `NONCE` as its first line and by the §7.2 refusal words.
decisions.why: Every node sends 1 today and only PlayMap compares it (PeerTable.cs:134). The first draft's 'keeps 1.3 in full' would have been false on the day every node first sent 3.
decisions.alternatives: 'Keeps 1.3 in full' (the first draft); caps only.

decisions.decision: Limits are sender maxima that every reader accepts. Hello: at most 1200 B sent, at least 2048 B read; 32 caps of [a-z0-9.-]{1,24}; t [a-z0-9_-]{1,16}; id [A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,40}; inst 8 hex; name and host at most 64 characters, read whole; at most 8 ports; 128 peers. Context: 64 KiB counted in UTF-8 bytes; 200 items; 400 links (each end at most 120 characters); 20 recent; 256 commands; 32 peers. A reader keeps a verb (up to 512) whole or drops it, and keeps at least 200 characters of words. A reader that keeps commands keeps at least 256; a view of them may show fewer, saying how many it left out. Over 64 KiB a sender trims in a fixed order: recent lines, then links, then commands other than panic, air and transport, then grey and green items. It never trims reds, ambers or panic, air and transport commands, and adds one grey item, context:trimmed.
decisions.why: Measured: Patterns writes 200 items (ShowContext.cs:68,180). PlayMap's busy context is 38,142 B compact and about 47.5 KB at 256 commands. PlayMap's owner set at least 256 where a reader caps (Mapper/docs/round3/PLAN.md:2594-2610). The byte limit binds before the per-field limits do.
decisions.alternatives: One shared number for senders and readers, which breaks the strictest reader on the day a node grows. The first draft's 128 items, which would have made Patterns non-conforming.

decisions.decision:
Where a hello goes:
- A networked node broadcasts it from a socket bound to its doors' address.
- It may also send a copy to 127.0.0.1, which no reader relies on.
- A node bound to loopback only sends no hello.
- `ports` names only doors every receiver can open.
- The carrier for apps on one machine with no network is lab line LB-1 (Windows 11: 127.0.0.1, 127.255.255.255 and loopback multicast, with the network up and off). 1.4 names it.
decisions.why: Measured here and in ecosystem-lane: a unicast to a shared port reaches exactly one listener, and a 127.0.0.1-bound socket (PlayMap's, HelloService.cs:124-125) takes all of them. A broadcast fails with ENETUNREACH when only loopback is up. AGMessage's any-bound socket sends a loopback copy that its LAN-bound HOST cannot answer (server.js:44,1003-1005; nodes.js:91,95).
decisions.alternatives: Loopback-only hellos (the first draft): one app of several finds the node, at random. 127.255.255.255 now: unmeasured on Windows and missed by 127.0.0.1-bound listeners.

decisions.decision:
One id is one peer.
- A reader keeps every address it heard in the last 6 s and keeps dialling the address in use while it is still heard. An address change alone raises no event.
- A peer on this machine may be dialled at 127.0.0.1 first, falling back to the heard address. Host-name equality alone is not enough.
- Typed-address lookups match any heard address or the host.
- Every node sends `inst`. Alternating inst values A, B, A within 6 s (or two hosts, for a node with no inst) mark the id as a conflict: amber, never merged, no new link, cleared after 60 s.
decisions.why: Stops the per-beat address flip whichever listener got the copy. Keeps AGMessage's find, pin key and desk detection (nodes.js:108-113,247-252,413-416). Makes a cloned install visible. A second address alone would wrongly flag a node with two network interfaces.
decisions.alternatives: Prefer loopback (the first draft): nondeterministic, and wrong for AGMessage's LAN HOST. Flag any second address: false alarms on a node with two interfaces.

decisions.decision:
Reads after pairing is the contract rule (§1 rule 4 built around each node's public view; §7.2 for line wires). Each node reaches it by its own decision, and §8 lists exemptions with what ends them.
- Patterns Round 90.2 happens only if its maintainer agrees (ADR-016, reversing PLAN §103.7), in one of two scopes. Scope A holds back the STATE greeting, the pushes and STATE/STATUS/CONTEXT/SUBSCRIBE until pairing, while named queries stay open. Scope B holds back every query.
- Prerequisites: the module pairs before it reads; WirePeer keeps the pairing and every push re-checks it; an inventory of the desk's own cross-machine asks; six test files rewritten; the Super Check Remote row; a log line.
- It waits for playout-links' PlayoutLink, which shows a token-less link amber.
- PlayMap's TCP read is a question to its owner (decision 17), not a unit.
decisions.why: Every claim was verified. The module asks NAV before NONCE (main.js:150-164). NodesService and ServiceKernel ask without pairing (NodesService.cs:149-227; ServiceKernel.cs:97-101). `presented` is a local variable (ControlService.cs:369) and Broadcast pushes to everyone (:763-774). The tests assert today's order (ShowBusAppTests.cs:71-82; RemoteTrustTests.cs:132-150). Stagewatch's current link with no token reports green (PatternsLink.cs:202,210,291-295).
decisions.alternatives: A permanent open-read tier (PLAN §103.7's stance). It stays open to the Patterns maintainer through the ADR.

decisions.decision: A certificate's whole span, NotBefore to NotAfter, is at most 825 days. NotBefore is at most 24 h back, and NotAfter is computed from NotBefore. At start-up a node makes a new certificate when fewer than 30 days remain or when its current span is over 825 days. Each tree's papers announce the one CERTIFICATE CHANGED that pinned peers will see.
decisions.why: Fixing only the code would leave Patterns' 1,826-day certificates in place for five years (ShowBusTls.cs:83,106). Stagewatch's are 826 days (NodeCertificate.cs:66) and AGMessage's 825 days plus 1 h (tls.js:78-79).
decisions.alternatives: Key-continuity rollover, left for 1.4. Fixing only new certificates, which leaves the iPad problem in place.

decisions.decision:
Windows: this area writes §12.1-12.3 and rule 5's view-pass class. View passes are counted apart from credentials: a correct PIN or key never clears the view-pass count.
- windows-for-peers writes §12.4 onwards (grants, the black end, held forms, placement claims, the operator-frame windows block), rule 5's carrier exemption (its D0) and the caps pages and window-draw.
- Dropped: leases, windows.lend, web.show, window.join, Authorization: Window, and units S5/S7/S8 of the first draft.
- Asked of windows-for-peers: grants only from doors that authenticate the operator (never OSC or an unauthenticated Companion TCP); D4's loopback dial falls back to the heard address and never relies on host name alone; the `windows` cap lands in S2's builder.
decisions.why: Two verbs with two security postures in one contract. windows-for-peers already sends the whole grants list each time a link opens, which reconciles them. One lockout table that a correct key clears (WebServer.cs:35,625-642,1083) is a deterministic flaw. OSC has no PIN (OscServer.cs:7-14; AppSettings.cs:270).
decisions.alternatives: Keep leases (the first draft): contradicts windows-for-peers on every point.

decisions.decision:
Copies are held by a hash plus §13's machine-read block.
- The body is defined exactly: UTF-8 with no BOM, CRLF turned to LF, exactly one final LF.
- Each tree's test catches accidental edits and checks every §13 number that tree implements. Stale copies are caught only by tools/showbus-copies.sh in G44's interop lane, and the header says so.
- A node may send caps declared in its own node page's showbus-node block.
- §9 says 'The language model'. PlayMap gets a copy.
decisions.why: Each CI checks out only its own tree, and PlayMap cannot edit its bus files during round 3 (Mapper/docs/round3/PLAN.md:2122-2125).
decisions.alternatives: Fetching the master in CI, or a git submodule.

decisions.decision: NODES.md is rewritten from Stagewatch's code and held by a test that its hello example is what the builder makes. The 9700 Find stays until Patterns L47 is walked.
decisions.why: G41: NODES.md has been stale since 2.11.1.

decisions.decision: AGMessage keeps its `proposals` cap and its 1-second ping; its papers say 'every second'.
decisions.why: No reader branches on the cap name, and renaming it costs a test change (tls.test.js:82).

decisions.decision: `presenting` stays in the hello, named as the one show fact a hello carries: a Slides agent's boolean that other agents' windows show.
decisions.why: Rule 4 and the field table must agree. SlidesAgentWindow.xaml.cs:113 is its only reader.
decisions.alternatives: Drop it, which loses the agent window's only source.

revised.wire:
HELLO (UDP 9928, every 2 s, no authentication, no secret)

Example:
{"t":"main","v":1,"proto":3,"id":"3f9c2a1b7d0e","inst":"a41f09c2","name":"Hall A","host":"FOH-PC","ports":{"http":9924,"https":9924,"ws":9924},"caps":["timer","cues","messages","context","receipts","clock","screens","windows","aux","slides-in","copilot","approvals","mcp"],"clock":1760101234567,"tls":"sha256:<64hex>"}

Fields:
- v: 1.
- proto: 3, the revision whose shapes the node speaks.
- t: [a-z0-9_-]{1,16}. Kinds: main (Stagewatch), agent (Stagewatch Slides), patterns, playmap (PlayMap), messenger (AGMessage).
- id: [A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,40}.
- inst (new for Stagewatch and AGMessage; Patterns and PlayMap already send it): 8 lowercase hex, new at each process start.
- name and host: at most 64 characters each.
- ports: at most 8, from {http, https, ws, wire, osc, companion, sync}.
- caps: at most 32, each [a-z0-9.-]{1,24}.
- tls: sha256:<64 lowercase hex>.
- presenting: Slides agent only.
- Size: at most 1200 B sent; readers accept at least 2048 B, keep at least 32 caps and keep names whole.

Sending:
- Sent from a socket bound to the address the node's doors listen on.
- A networked node sends to 255.255.255.255:9928, plus an optional copy to 127.0.0.1:9928; each send has its own try.
- A node bound to loopback only sends nothing.
- `ports` lists only doors every receiver can open. Stagewatch names companion and osc only when they are bound to the network.

Hearing:
- At most 128 peers, forgotten after 60 s.
- Per id, every address heard in the last 6 s is kept. The dial address is sticky while it is still heard.
- A same-machine peer may be dialled at 127.0.0.1 first, falling back to the heard address.
- An address change alone raises no event.
- Conflict: inst A, then B, then A within 6 s (or two hosts, for a node with no inst). The peer shows amber, both hosts and addresses are named, no new link is dialled, and the mark clears after 60 s.

Caps vocabulary (§13):
- main: timer, cues, messages, context, receipts, clock, screens, windows, aux, slides-in, copilot, approvals, mcp.
- agent: slides.
- patterns: video, video.clock, video.transport, video.seek, video.end, state, eye, context, receipts, clock, pages.
- playmap: the same video and state set as patterns, plus mcp, playlist, media, mapping, scan, show, window-draw.
- messenger: messages, action-prompts, documents, ai, context, receipts, proposals.
- Reserved: video.anchor.
- A node may also send caps declared in its node page's showbus-node block.

CONTEXT (§6)
Limits:
- At most 64 KiB, counted in UTF-8 bytes.
- items ≤ 200; links ≤ 400 (each end ≤ 120 characters); recent ≤ 20; commands ≤ 256; peers ≤ 32.
- headline ≤ 200; item id / kind / label / state ≤ 60 / 30 / 80 / 160; recent line ≤ 200; verb ≤ 512; words ≤ 512.

Readers:
- A reader keeps a verb whole or drops it and counts the drop, and keeps at least 200 characters of words.
- A reader that keeps commands keeps at least 256. A view of them shows panic, air and transport rows first and says how many it left out.

Trimming, when a context is over 64 KiB, in this order:
1. the oldest recent lines;
2. grey links, then the other links;
3. commands other than panic, air and transport, from the end;
4. grey items, then green items.
Reds, ambers and the panic, air and transport commands are never trimmed. The sender then adds:
{"id":"context:trimmed","kind":"health","label":"Context","light":"grey","state":"left out: 12 recent, 40 links, 30 commands, 5 items"}

Posting: POST /api/peers/context on change, at least every 10 s while linked, at most once a second. The desk keeps a context 30 s and answers a too-large context with 413 and its size (that 413 is cross-app-proposals SW-1).

READS AFTER PAIRING (§7.2: line wires Patterns 9697 and PlayMap 9941, on a token node, from a connection the node does not trust)
- The first line is `NONCE <32 hex>`. Nothing of the show is sent before pairing.
- Answered before pairing: HELLO, NONCE, AUTH-PROOF, PING, HELP, VERBS, plus the node's §8-named open queries. Under Patterns' scope A these are NAV, MENU, CUE LIST, ARCADE … and ASSISTANT ….
- Anything else gets `ERR [@id] not paired — this node shows its state only to a paired connection`.
- `AUTH-PROOF <hex>` (HMAC-SHA256(token, nonce + hello name)) gets `OK [@id] paired`. `STATE {json}` then follows at once and on every change, and stops when the token changes.
- An open node (no token) greets with STATE as in 1.2.
- A reader sends its reads only after `OK paired` / `OK open`. With no token it shows amber "not paired — <node> shows its state only to a paired link; its pairing token goes in <where>" and sends only PING.
- HTTP and WS are unchanged: anything beyond the public view needs a key, token or PIN.

CERTIFICATES (§10)
- ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256.
- NotAfter − NotBefore ≤ 825 days; NotBefore no earlier than creation − 24 h.
- A new certificate is made at start-up when fewer than 30 days remain or the span is over 825 days. Peers see CERTIFICATE CHANGED once.
- hello `tls` and ports.https are unchanged.

WINDOWS (§12.1-12.3 here; §12.4 onwards belongs to windows-for-peers)
- Address /w/<token>: 26 characters of abcdefghijkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789; at most 64 windows per node.
- View passes (window addresses, viewing codes, crew links) are counted per device apart from PINs and keys. 5 wrong in a minute lock out view passes only, and a correct PIN or key never clears that count.
- The address is listed only to the PIN or a control key.
- The window link is as built in 2.17:
  - /ws?win=<token>[&detail=1];
  - server to window: {"type":"window",id,name,content,hold,holdText,holdImage,onLoss,fadeMs,rev}, {"type":"identify",name,id}, {"type":"reload"}, {"type":"window","revoked":true};
  - window to server: {"type":"shown",rev,content,hold,ms,error}.
- Rule 5's carrier exemption and the grants messages are windows-for-peers' words (its D0, a maintainer's call).

§13 BLOCK (in the hashed body, machine-read)
- Lines of the form `key value…`, for example: hello.bytes 1200, hello.read.bytes 2048, hello.caps 32, hello.name.chars 64, hello.inst.chars 8, peers.max 128, peer.conflict.clear.ms 60000, context.bytes 65536, context.items 200, context.links 400, context.link.end.chars 120, context.commands 256, context.verb.chars 512, context.words.read.chars 200, cert.days 825, cert.renew.days 30, window.token.chars 26, view.wrong.per.minute 5, window.grants 4.
- Plus the kind, port, cap and reserved rows.

STAGEWATCH
- Context item `bus:hello` (kind health, amber) appears when every hello target has failed for 3 beats: "this Stagewatch's hello can't go out: <words> — other apps can't find it". A failed broadcast alone is not amber.
- Show network line:
  - "Said on the network as <name> (<id>)";
  - "Said on this PC only — no network: <words>";
  - "Not said: <words>";
  - "Not said — Remote is set to this PC; other apps reach it at 127.0.0.1:<port>".
- Peer rows in conflict are amber.
- Rig: new flags `--bus <listen port>` and `--bus-to <host:port>`.
- No new verb, endpoint, Companion action or frame field.

PATTERNS (Round 90.2, if the maintainer agrees)
- The Companion module sends NAV, MENU and RECORD only after OK paired. AUTH-PROOF goes through ask.
- With no token and a NONCE heard, the module's status reads "pairing token needed — this desk shows its state only to a paired connection".
- One log line per connection when an unpaired read is refused.
- Super Check's Remote row reads "reads follow pairing on the wire".

COPY HEADER
"*<App>'s copy of the Show Bus contract, 1.3 (body sha256 <64 hex>). The master is Stagewatch's docs/SHOWBUS.md; where they differ, the master wins. How <App> implements it: <its page>.*"
The body runs from `## 1. Rules every node follows` to the end: UTF-8 with no BOM, LF line ends, exactly one final LF.

changes.change: Pure builder: Main(nodeId, inst, name, machine, HelloDoors, mcp, clock) returns (Hello?, HelloScope{None, Network}). Scope None when WebBindAll is off. Ports list only network-bound doors. Proto 3; inst; windows and mcp caps; names cut to 64. Also Targets(scope, port), CapShape and NewInst.
The agent hello carries Proto 3 and an inst (:72).
The hello is built by ShowBusHello.Main from _store.Snapshot and the servers' running ports and binds, not live Settings (:21-48). The scope is passed to the beacon. Exposes the Status line.
Amber bus:hello when every target fails for 3 beats; conflict rows amber with both hosts; the kind label from ShowBusKinds.Label (:100).
Label(kind) from §13's kind rows (playmap → PlayMap).
Stagewatch's own context stays within §6: at most 200 items, the byte-trimming order, a context:trimmed item with counts. Reds, ambers and panic, air and transport commands are never trimmed.

Span 825 days; backdate 1 day; Window(now) returns (NotBefore, NotBefore + Span). NeedsRenewal is true when fewer than 30 days remain or the span is over 825 days. NodeCertificate.cs:34 and :66 use it.

A second table, _passFailures, counts view passes (window addresses, viewing codes, crew links); LockedOut and CountFailure (:625-636) use it. Authorize's success (:1083) clears only the credentials table.
--bus <listen port> and --bus-to <host:port>: the hello is built from the rig's servers and --bind, and sent to the override target.

LB-1: binds sockets (any and 127.0.0.1, ReuseAddress) on one port, sends to 127.0.0.1, 127.255.255.255, 255.255.255.255 and 239.255.99.28 on loopback, and prints who heard what. Run on the maintainer's Windows PC with the network up and off.
Header and body hashes for each tree; diff against the master; exit 1 on a mismatch; 'not run' for an absent tree. Used by ecosystem-lane's S7.2 row.

Rewritten from the code (builder hello example held by a test; scope; hearing, sticky dial and conflict; Find on 9928 plus 9700 until L47; public versus keyed reads; the links as built; AGMessage; PlayMap; pointer to §13).

ECOSYSTEM names PlayMap and 1.3. REMOTE 2.18 covers the hello, hearing and conflict, the two lockout counts, and the certificate span with its one renewal. FEATURES gets the Show network hello line. WHATS_NEXT gets LB-1, rollover, ?pin= and 9923 as not scheduled.
ADR-016, 'The wire shows its state only to a paired connection', reversing PLAN §103.7 with scope A or B. The maintainer's call, written before any code.

AUTH-PROOF goes through ask, and NAV, RECORD ON and reads are asked after OK paired / OK open (:150-164, :196-206). With no token and a NONCE heard, the status words. trustProblem (:373) tells 'no token configured' from 'wrong token'.
The Wire helpers read NONCE first and STATE after pairing on a distrusted token desk. The STATUS-unpaired assertion is inverted. The other files that set TrustLoopback = false are checked.

Round 90.5: Life is 825 days counted as the whole span, CreateSelfSigned(utcNow.AddDays(-1), utcNow.AddDays(-1) + Life) (:84,103). NeedsRenewal is also true when the span is over Life (:106). Comment :77.

issues.issue: The loopback hello reaches only one app. Decision 5 (loopback-only scope), decision 6 (loopback-first hearing), §2 'Where a hello goes' and the G27 fix all assume a datagram sent to 127.0.0.1:9928 reaches every app on the laptop. It does not. When several sockets share a port through SO_REUSEADDR or SO_REUSEPORT, a unicast datagram is delivered to exactly one of them. So on a Wi-Fi-off show laptop, a loopback-only Stagewatch is found by at most one app, and possibly only by its own listener. Loopback-first hearing becomes nondeterministic for the same reason. The planned tests stand on the same flaw. In bus.e2e.cjs the rig's own SlidesBeacon binds the port the e2e listens on, so which socket hears the hello is a race. The G27 live test fails the same way if its target port is also the beacon's listen port.
issues.evidence:
Measured in the scratchpad.
- Python, three SO_REUSEADDR sockets on 0.0.0.0:29928, five unicasts to 127.0.0.1: one socket received all five, the other two none; a 255.255.255.255 and a 127.255.255.255 send reached all three (critique-spec13/udp.py).
- .NET 10 UdpClient with ReuseAddress, three sockets: one received all six loopback unicasts, the others none; a broadcast reached all three (critique-spec13/udpnet/u.cs).
- The sibling design ecosystem-lane.md:199-213 measured the same thing and flagged it to spec-1-3 at :1171-1174.
- SlidesBeacon binds its receiver to the port it is given (RemoteSlides.cs:150), and its timer sends to that same port.
- The Windows documentation calls unicast delivery to a shared port indeterminate.
issues.fix: Keep §2 from naming 127.0.0.1 as the carrier until a Windows lab line measures it. Candidates are 127.255.255.255 (reaches every any-bound listener on Linux, but not a 127.0.0.1-bound one) or multicast on the loopback interface with IP_MULTICAST_LOOP. Until then, write loopback-only scope as 'may stay silent', which is today's behaviour. In tests, send to a port that only the test socket binds: the targets override must differ from the beacon's listen port, and bus.e2e must not share 19928 with the rig's listener.

issues.issue: Unit P2 (reads only after pairing) breaks Patterns' own Companion module even when the module has the right token. On connect the module sends HELLO and then immediately `ask('NAV')`, before the NONCE arrives and before it can send AUTH-PROOF. It asks NAV only once per connection. Under P2 that NAV is answered `ERR not paired …`, so the Navigator gets no rails or pages for the whole connection. trustProblem matches that line and puts the module into BadConfig with words saying the token is missing, although it is configured. This disproves decision 7's premise that every reader that matters already pairs first, and P2's module change, which only adds status words, does not fix it.
issues.evidence:
- Patterns/integrations/companion-module-patterns/src/main.js:150-164: HELLO, then NAV at connect, with the token answered only later by authenticate().
- main.js:196-206: authenticate() sets `authed` before `OK paired` arrives.
- main.js:215-224: an ERR line goes through trustProblem and sets BadConfig.
- main.js:275-287: ask() sends no request id, so the ERR is a bare `ERR not paired` that the regex at :373 matches.
- IsQuery treats NAV and MENU as reads (ControlProtocol.cs:1454).
issues.fix: P2 must change the module so that NAV, MENU and every other read go out after `OK paired`, or are re-asked when it arrives. Add a module node test where a token desk sends NONCE first and the Navigator still fills. Make trustProblem tell apart 'no token configured' from 'asked before pairing'.

issues.issue:
Unit P2 breaks Patterns' own readers that talk to other machines, and its existing tests, which assert the opposite on purpose. The design says 'STATE's shape is unchanged … tests keep working' and only adds tests.
- Every fresh desk has a token.
- The desk's NodesService asks arcade nodes `ARCADE STATUS/GAMES/SCORES` over their wire without pairing.
- A node asks the desk `ASSISTANT MODERATE` without pairing. Both are queries today, so P2 refuses both.
- RemoteTrustTests asserts that reading never needs the token.
- The Wire helpers in ShowBusAppTests and RemoteTrustTests assert `STATE {` as the first line, then NONCE, with TrustLoopback=false and a token set; P2 turns that order around.
- NEW TOKEN must now cut reads, not just verbs. But the token a connection presented is a local variable in the connection handler, and Broadcast pushes to every WirePeer, so 'Broadcast skips unpaired peers' needs that pairing state moved onto WirePeer and checked again at each push.
- P2 reverses a documented maintainer decision (PLAN §103.7, REMOTE Trust) without an ADR entry.
issues.evidence:
- Patterns/tests/Patterns.App.Tests/ShowBusAppTests.cs:241-247 (paired from first run) and :71-82 (greeting STATE then NONCE).
- RemoteTrustTests.cs:132-150: `Assert.StartsWith("OK {", …)  // reading never needs the token`.
- NodesService.cs:120-160 (unpaired asks); ServiceKernel.cs:97 (`ASSISTANT MODERATE` sent to a desk); ControlProtocol.cs:1249 and :1454 (queries).
- ControlService.cs:367 (`presented` is a local); :763-774 (Broadcast pushes to every peer).
- docs/PLAN.md:11648-11654; docs/REMOTE.md:38-41.
issues.fix:
Before P2:
- Inventory Patterns' wire clients that cross machines. Make them pair, or name each one as an exemption.
- List the tests to rewrite: the greeting order in the Wire helpers and the RemoteTrustTests :132 case inverted.
- Store each connection's pairing on WirePeer and re-check it on every push, so NEW TOKEN stops STATE.
- Write an ADR entry and present P2 as a maintainer's call, not a settled unit.

issues.issue: The design's risk note says loopback-first hearing never picks loopback for a peer that does not listen there, because 'such a peer sends no loopback hello'. That is false for AGMessage. Its HTTP listens on HOST, which can be a single LAN address. Its UDP socket is bound to any address and sends to both 255.255.255.255 and 127.0.0.1 whenever it announces, and it announces whenever HOST is not loopback. So the loopback copy arrives from 127.0.0.1. A loopback-first reader then dials 127.0.0.1:<port> and is refused for as long as it keeps hearing that copy.
issues.evidence:
- AGMessage/app/server.js:44 and :1245 (listen on HOST); :1003-1005 (announce = HOST is not loopback).
- nodes.js:91 (socket bound to any address) and :95 (`for (const to of ['255.255.255.255','127.0.0.1'])`).
- By contrast, Patterns' hello socket is bound to its bind address (BeaconService.cs:96-97 and :311-324), and PlayMap's sender binds `bind ?? Any` (HelloService.cs:136-137), so neither has this problem.
issues.fix: Make it a contract rule: a node sends the loopback copy only when its doors listen on loopback (bound to any address or to loopback), or sends it from a socket bound to its bind address. A1 implements this in AGMessage and tests it with a LAN HOST.

issues.issue: Loopback-first hearing breaks AGMessage's lookup of its Stagewatch peer, its TLS pin and its approval-desk detection on a single laptop. find() matches a peer only when its address equals the operator's typed host, or when its host name matches. With loopback-first, a same-machine Stagewatch is stored at 127.0.0.1, so an operator who typed the laptop's LAN IP no longer matches. The pin key then falls back from `node:<id>` to `url:<host>:<port>`, which pins again under a new key. The hello's `tls` no longer upgrades the link, and checkDesk loses the `approvals` cap.
issues.evidence: AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:108-113 (find: `p.address === host`), :247-252 (_resolve: nodeKey and wantTls taken from the found peer), :413-416 (checkDesk reads `peer.caps`).
issues.fix: Keep every address heard for an id, each with its age, and match find against any of them. Keep the choice of which address to dial separate from the peer's identity. Test with an operator-typed LAN IP while the hello arrives on loopback.

issues.issue: 'One id is one peer; an address change alone is not a change' removes the only signal that two machines claim the same id. Ids are unauthenticated, and the id files travel with settings when a show laptop is imaged or a folder is copied. Today the flip-flop at least raises Changed or onChange; the design suppresses it and silently merges the two machines.
issues.evidence:
- Patterns keeps its id in a patterns.node-id file (ShowBusNetwork.cs:191-203); Stagewatch in Settings.NodeId; AGMessage in settings.nodeId (server.js:82).
- PlayMap raises Changed on an address change (PeerTable.cs:63-65); AGMessage calls onChange when the address differs (nodes.js:89).
issues.fix: Add to §2: an id heard from two different non-loopback addresses within the stale window is a conflict, shown amber ('two machines say they are <id>'), never merged. Stagewatch, Patterns, PlayMap and AGMessage each test it.

issues.issue: Leases are not reconciled, and the shared lockout turns one stale lessee into a lockout of every app on the laptop. An end message is pushed only on a live link, and the link sends only 'lend again on open'. A lessee that was offline when the window was revoked or deleted keeps dialling the dead /w/ address. Wrong window addresses count in the same per-IP table as wrong PINs, keys and viewing codes. With loopback-first every same-laptop app is 127.0.0.1, so five 404s a minute lock out AGMessage's key, Patterns' link and the operator's local PIN. Separately, a successful key from that IP clears the counter, which weakens the 'five wrong tries a minute' guarantee §12.2 promises.
issues.evidence:
- Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:35 (one `_authFailures` table), :625-642 (window lockout and counting), :873-886 (PIN), :1076-1084 (keys; `TryRemove` on success).
- windows-for-peers.md:150-152 (decision 8: tombstones, from this measured cause).
issues.fix: On link open, send the lessee its complete set of current leases, and have it drop any it holds that are not in the set. Tombstone withdrawn addresses so a guess there does not count. Keep separate lockout counters for window addresses and for credentials. Test that a revoke while the lessee is offline ends the lease on its next link.

issues.issue:
`window lend` is an escalation path in four ways.
- The parser accepts `all` as the window, so `window lend all X` hands over every window's address in one line, and the refusal list does not cover it.
- OSC is unauthenticated and, once switched on, binds to every interface by default. Companion TCP has no authentication when it is bound to the network. So anyone who can send UDP could hand passes to any key-verified node, turning a node-scope key, which today never sees a path, into a holder of window passes.
- ShowContext.Commands publishes the verb to peers' AIs, so a peer can propose lending a window to itself.
- Lending by name is ambiguous when two nodes share a name.
issues.evidence:
- ShowState.cs:931-941 (`who` may be `all`); OscServer.cs:7-14 (shared grammar, no PIN); AppSettings.cs:270 (OscBindAll defaults to true).
- WebServer.cs:679 (a path only for the PIN or a control key); ShowContext.cs:41-43 (the window rows peers read).
issues.fix: Refuse `all` and ambiguous names. Accept lend and unlend only from the desk, the PIN or a control key, and refuse them on OSC and Companion TCP. Do not list lend in ShowContext.Commands, or refuse a proposal from node X that lends to X. The approval card says 'hands lobby's address to <node>'.

issues.issue:
The meaning given to `proto` contradicts itself. proto 3 is defined as 'keeps 1.3 in full', yet the design's own §8 exemptions and unit order mean no node that sends 3 keeps 1.3 in full:
- Stagewatch sends 3 from S2, while `?pin=` and an unauthenticated Companion port 9923 remain, and no unit adds the '2.18 warns' that §8 promises.
- PlayMap sends 3 from M1, but keeps §7.2 only after M2.
- Patterns enforces §7.2 in P2 while still sending proto 1 until P3.
- AGMessage still drops unknown kinds (G18), so its §8 row's 'none' is wrong.

The justification that a reader can tell 'shows nothing before pairing on purpose' from 'broken' therefore cannot work.

- AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:33 and :38 (KINDS drops playmap).

issues.issue:
The §6 numbers disagree with the sibling design and with the PlayMap owner's recorded decisions.
- cross-app-proposals caps `words` at 200 on the sender; spec-1-3 says 512 on the sender and at least 200 kept by a reader. PlayMap's busy context has 13 commands whose `words` exceed 200.
- §6 lets a reader that feeds a prompt keep fewer commands than 256. The owner's decision 18 says that where a reader caps, the cap is at least 256. The design claims to adopt that item.
- §5.6 item 7 and decision 17 keep PlayMap's reader bounds as its own and keep Patterns reading PlayMap's context over the wire 'as today'. M2 and its §8 end condition commit PlayMap's owner to closing that read.
issues.evidence:

- Mapper/docs/round3/PLAN.md:2594-2610 (decisions 17 and 18) and :2333-2340 (§5.6 item 7).

issues.issue: The size limits cannot all be met at once, and only items have a trimming rule. With every field at its maximum, 256 commands of up to 512+512 characters alone are several times 64 KiB. §6 says how to trim items (`context:trimmed`) but not commands, links or bytes. Stagewatch rejects a whole context over 64 KB, so a large post is lost entirely rather than shortened. PlayMap's busy context is already 43.6 KB with 199 commands, about 165 bytes each; at 215 to 256 commands it reaches roughly 46-53 KB before any extra items.
issues.evidence:
- Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ShowBus.cs:62 (`json.Length is 0 or > MaxBytes` rejects the whole post).
- Measured from the golden file: 43,640 bytes, of which commands are 32,958.
issues.fix: Give §6 a byte-trimming order (recent lines, then links, then commands other than air and panic, then grey items), with a count of what was left out. Measure PlayMap's context after round 3 against 64 KiB before fixing the number.

issues.issue:
Stagewatch's own reader would still break §6 when S9 declares 1.3 final, and the per-tree tests do not check most numbers.
- Stagewatch's reader cuts `verb` to 80 characters and keeps 64 commands; §6 says a reader never cuts a verb. The command change belongs to another area's unit, and S9 does not wait for it.
- Stagewatch and AGMessage cut hello names and hosts at 60 characters, below the 64 senders may use.
- Patterns keeps 64 commands.
- Patterns, PlayMap and AGMessage have no 128-peer bound, although §2 states one.
- No tree checks its own context against the sender maxima.

- AGMessage nodes.js:44 (name and host sliced to 60); Patterns ShowContext.cs:99.

issues.issue: Fixing the certificate code does not fix certificates already issued. Every node renews only when NotAfter comes within 30 days. So Patterns' existing 1,826-day certificates stay for about five years, and the iPad problem P1 targets remains on every existing install. The design says the contract 'should leave no room to find out on show day' and then leaves this room open.

- Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ShowBusTls.cs:83 (Life of 5 × 365 days) and :106 (NeedsRenewal looks at NotAfter only).
- Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/NodeCertificate.cs:34 (renewal by NotAfter only).
issues.fix: Also renew at start when NotAfter − NotBefore is more than cert.days. Peers see one CERTIFICATE CHANGED, which each tree's papers announce. Test that an old 1,826-day certificate is replaced.

issues.issue:
The hash fence is oversold as 'a copy that cannot drift'.
- Each tree's test compares its copy only with the constant pinned in that tree.
- Each CI checks out only its own repository. A master revision leaves the copies stale while every tree stays green; only tools/showbus-copies.sh on a bench sees it.
- The vocabulary check makes a cap that one tree adds fail that tree's build until the master and three copies change. PlayMap cannot even edit its bus files during round 3, so a small feature in one tree waits on four release processes.
- Line endings are normalised, but a BOM or a missing final newline would still change the hash.
issues.evidence:
- Each repository's CLAUDE.md describes CI on its own tree only.
- Mapper/docs/round3/PLAN.md:2122-2125 ('nothing in that wave edits it').
- spec-1-3.md:216-227.
issues.fix: Say it plainly: the per-tree test stops accidental edits, and only the interop lane catches stale copies. Let a node send caps of its own, declared on its node page, without failing the vocabulary check. Define the body bytes exactly: strip any BOM and end with exactly one LF.

issues.issue:
P2 and M2 have consequences in Stagewatch and in Patterns' wider surfaces that no unit covers.
- Stagewatch's PatternsLink with no token reports green 'connected' at once. Because an empty token counts as 'proof sent', it sends `@ctx CONTEXT` every 5 s. After P2 the link is green but receives nothing, with an ERR every 5 s. That breaks Stagewatch's 'observed state over sent state'. No S unit implements §7.2's amber words on a reader.
- Patterns' doctrines: the health lights must say what pairing does not cover, Super Check's Remote row must change, and the closing check must be a journal row, a log line or a Super Check row. The design names the wire's refusal line instead.
issues.evidence:
- Stagewatch/src/Timer.Integrations/PatternsLink.cs:202 (`_proofSent = _token.Length == 0`), :210 (reports Ok 'connected'), :291-295 (`@ctx CONTEXT` every 5 s).
- Patterns/CLAUDE.md: the standing brief's closing sentence and the doctrine 'the health lights say what pairing does not cover'.
- Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md:30 (Super Check's Remote row).
issues.fix: Before P2 lands, add a Stagewatch unit or a stated dependency on playout-links: a link that heard NONCE and has no token shows amber with the §7.2 words and sends nothing more. P2's papers name the Super Check row and add a journal or log line for an unpaired read that is refused.

issues.issue: §12 contradicts itself and Stagewatch's own doctrine. §12.3 says a node link never carries a window address, while §12.4 sends the lease `url` on that very link. Stagewatch's doctrine says window addresses ride in no frame.
issues.evidence:
- spec-1-3.md:400 against :404-408.
- Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md doctrine: 'the PIN, keys and window addresses ride in no log line, no journal row and no frame'.
issues.fix: If leases survive the reconciliation with windows-for-peers, name the lease message as the one point-to-point carrier: never a published frame, never journaled. Add a fence test that the address appears in no published frame.

issues.issue: Over-building: S7 and §12.6 (a node joining as a window with an `Authorization: Window` header, reserved cap `window.join`) have no consumer. The window link carries Stagewatch page paths, which a native node cannot draw, PlayMap has no browser engine, and the existing `?win=` parameter already works for any WebSocket client.
issues.evidence:
- ScreenWindows.cs:20 (content is a page path such as `/clock?h=12`).
- WebServer.cs:1145-1150 (`?win=` is the window link's pass).
- windows-for-peers.md:132-137 ('PlayMap has no browser'; `how:"draw"` replaces the header).
issues.fix: Drop S7, §12.6 and `window.join`.

issues.issue: The new `bus:hello` amber item would light permanently on the design's own commonest rig. With 'Allow other devices' on but Wi-Fi off, the scope is Network: the broadcast fails with ENETUNREACH every beat while the loopback copy goes out. The item would say 'other apps can't find it', which is not true.
issues.evidence:
- ecosystem-lane.md:203 (255.255.255.255 gives ENETUNREACH when only loopback is up).
- spec-1-3.md:575-578 (the 3-beat amber rule).
issues.fix: Count failures per target. Light amber only when every target fails, with words that fit the scope ('only this PC hears it').

issues.issue: Window lease text overflows its item, and lessee text reaches prompts. With up to 4 lessees, words like 'lent to Patterns FOH: Screen 2 — Foyer, on air' exceed the 160-character item state. The lessee's own `on.label` is copied into Stagewatch's context, which AIs read, so a peer's text enters a prompt.
issues.evidence: spec-1-3.md:416-419 (§12.5 state words) and :466 (`context.item.state.chars 160`).
issues.fix: Summarise more than one lessee ('lent to 2 apps') and list them in the operator frame. Cap and clean `on.label` the way other peer strings are cleaned.

issues.issue: Rule 4 is restated, but every Stagewatch hello still carries `presenting`. For a Slides agent that is show state, which rule 4 says discovery never carries.
issues.evidence: RemoteSlides.cs:112 (`presenting` field); SlidesAgent.cs:72 (`d is { Slide: > 0 }`).
issues.fix: Either name `presenting` in the §2 field table as an allowed exception, or drop it from the hello and leave it to the slide feed.
